Took the second option, on branch `fix/backlog-bootstate-verify` from `origin/main` at `35ca61d`. `docs/decisions/bootstate-partition-layouts.md` (accepted) records why the two layouts are distinct: they are not two offsets for one record. The userspace planes use an object-store partition (`contracts/store/disk/v1`, whose superblocks occupy LBA 0-1, the sectors boot-store v1 gives BootState), and the manager recognizes two constant identities rather than a directory of signed generations. The record makes boot-store v1 the only product layout and the LBA 1024/1025 layout test scaffolding. `docs/architecture/generation-management.md` cites it in its limits, and `docs/decisions/README.md` indexes it. Unifying the layouts, with the same-disk manager-then-selector plane the first option required, is the deferred item `01a0e54d-8a04-767d-95c5-0ded2ddc9a2d`.

Observed on 2026-09-28: `slime-root/src/boot_selector.rs` sets `STATE_SLOT_A/B = 0/1`; the manager and the rollback, recovery, and transfer probes set `1024/1025`; `boot-contracts/src/generated/store_disk.rs` sets `SLOT_A_LBA = 0`, `SLOT_B_LBA = 1`, and `RECORD_AREA_START = 2`. `just docs_check` passed (199 maintained documents), as did `just typos` and `just tasks_check`.

This is a documentation and decision change. No runtime test was run, and no code or on-disk layout changed. The limit it records still holds.
